original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Completeness of low templates, the simple Q3 path quotient, translated initial domains and bounded gap enumeration in the pinned connector-covering-code A/B representation, before capacity/propagation/search.
scope_change_reason: Follow PR3244's released search-domain handoff rather than repeating the independently implemented corrected seven-label census or its already-audited capacity/propagation predicates.
bottleneck_link: An exclusion requires complete candidate representation as well as sound pruning. This closes the named representation implication without repeating verified exclusions or extending a supplier search.
stop_rule: Stop after exact independent domain equality and the scoped representation proof, or a counterexample; no full B census, downstream implementation expansion or selected-frontier changes.
evidence: README.md proof; RESULT.json exact domain receipts; compiled original-source catalogues and explicit gap-loop instrumentation; four compiled semantic mutants and three stream/correspondence controls.
author: @krzysztofwojt
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in investigation, proof, implementation, checking and writing. A Luna worker performed read-only overlap extraction and an independent low-word/path enumeration, verified against the primary replay. No independent human or formal-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Does the actual branching and exhaustion reporting cover every represented candidate and every requested template without a lost branch or an unreported abort?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Domain completeness alone cannot turn a zero-hit or capped run into an exclusion.
open_questions.first_step: Compare Engine::search against a small explicit Cartesian-domain oracle with satisfying, unsatisfiable and interrupted cases; bind template IDs, flags and source hashes before independently replaying all B templates.
open_questions.blocked_by: The branching/exhaustion audit and a separately budgeted independent B run remain undone; other scoped proof premises remain separate.
